transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-08
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (CS), Laura (Sapphire - Head of Risk), Mateo (CISO), Karen (Procurement), Devon (Platform), Arjun (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Walkthrough of Sapphire Retail security questionnaire (combined SIG + customer form).
- Discussed SOC 2, ISO artifacts, RBAC/SSO, audit logs retention, KMS/HSM, data residency and private deployment options.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide SOC2 and KMS diagrams; customer to provide staging access for log samples; schedule deeper technical session.

Topics: SIG/CAIQ crosswalk, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, audit logs, KMS/HSM, data residency (EU), private vs hosted deployment, evidence packaging

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: All right thanks everyone for joining, uh we'll kick off, I'm Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE, and with me is Priya SE and Evan from CS. Um can we do quick intros from the Sapphire side?
[00:00:12] Laura: Hi this is Laura, head of vendor risk. We'll be driving the questionnaire.
[00:00:15] Mateo: Mateo CISO, security lead.
[00:00:18] Karen: Karen procurement, I'll own contract/evidence intake logistics.
[00:00:22] Devon: Devon platform, will be the hands-on for any infra access.
[00:00:26] Arjun: Arjun security analyst, here as well.
[00:00:30] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda — walk through the form items you flagged, call out where we have artifacts, and plan evidence delivery. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:00:40] Laura: Couple priorities — SOC 2, ISO artifacts if you have them, KMS policies, and we need audit log retention examples for compliance. Also data residency, we default to EU only for customer data.
[00:00:53] Priya: Yep, we can cover each. Quick note — some of your SIG items map directly to our CAIQ and SOC 2 answers; we'll point to the artifacts.

[00:01:08] Jordan: First question that often trips folks up — where customer data is stored by default and options. By default our hosted API stores data in region tied to customer account; we also have dedicated and private deployments for stricter residency.
[00:01:23] Devon: When you say private, do you mean VPC/VPN, or on-prem? We have a mandate that PII not leave EU for this workload.
[00:01:33] Priya: Good question. Private means customer-managed VPC + private control plane; also an on-prem package is possible for air-gapped scenarios. For EU-only we can pin the cluster to eu-west-1 region, or provision a private deployment in your EU VPC.
[00:01:49] Mateo: Is that something that incurs additional compliance reviews? Like we need to validate network diagrams and key management.
[00:01:56] Jordan: Yes, and we'll provide the architecture diagram, key separations, and KMS/HSM integration notes.

[00:02:10] Arjun: On KMS — are customers required to bring their own keys? How do you integrate with Okta or enterprise KMS/HSMs?
[00:02:17] Priya: We support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed KMS. For Private deployments you can integrate with your KMS via standard KMS APIs or HSMs. The transcript may show K M S as separate words — apologies. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer keys optional.
[00:02:31] Devon: If we use our KMS, can you provide the key policy and audit trail? We need to show key lifecycle controls.
[00:02:37] Priya: Absolutely — we can share key policy examples and the audit logs that show key usage.

[00:02:50] [00:02:50] Jordan: Moving to authentication and RBAC — question in the form about SSO and admin role separation. We support SAML SSO (Okta, ADFS) and granular RBAC, plus audit logs for admin actions.
[00:03:03] Laura: How granular is RBAC? Can we restrict model deployment and rollout permissions to a small set of users?
[00:03:09] Priya: Yes, you can scope by role: deploy, deploy+rollback, billing, read-only. Also token-level access controls so application tokens have narrower scopes.

[00:03:24] Mateo: Do you retain admin audit logs for at least 1 year? Our policy is 12 months immutable retention.
[00:03:30] Jordan: Our default retention is 90 days on hosted, but we have add-on retention packages that can do 1 year or longer for enterprise customers. For private/dedicated you can configure retention and ship logs to your S3 bucket.
[00:03:45] Karen: Ok so we'll need to document that as an add-on. Put that in the notes.

[00:03:55] [00:03:55] Arjun: On audit logs — what format and fields? We need user ID, action, timestamp, IP, resource identifier, and ideally request/response IDs for tracing.
[00:04:06] Priya: The audit schema includes actor, action, object, timestamp, request id, and context like IP and region. We'll attach a sample log export.
[00:04:15] Devon: Sample logs — can you provide sanitized examples so we can verify our SIEM ingestion?
[00:04:20] Priya: Yes we will provide a redacted sample and we can give a signed URL to a staging bucket.

[00:04:34] [00:04:34] Jordan: Regarding encryption at rest and in transit — we use TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit, at rest AES-256 with customer-managed keys option and HSM integration for Private deployments.
[00:04:48] Laura: For encryption evidence, what docs do you usually provide? Key rotation policy, KMS config, and certificate management?
[00:04:55] Priya: Correct — we'll provide rotation policy snapshots, KMS key policy excerpts, and cert lifecycle docs.

[00:05:06] [00:05:06] Jordan: Next — SIG/CAIQ mapping. A lot of your questions are SIG v2 items; we already maintain a CAIQ crosswalk that maps Redwood answers to SIG questions. We'll share that mapping so your Security team can cross-reference.
[00:05:19] Laura: Great. Does that include answers that reference SOC 2 controls or ISO controls?
[00:05:23] Priya: Yes, where applicable we map to SOC 2 control IDs and ISO 27001 Annex references.

[00:05:34] [00:05:34] Karen: Procurement question — what evidence format do you prefer? Single zip with index, or links? We need to keep our intake process clean.
[00:05:43] Jordan: Single indexed artifact usually works best — SOC2 redacted PDF, CAIQ spreadsheet, KMS snippets, diagrams in PNG/PDF, and sample logs as signed URLs. We'll coordinate with you on naming conventions.

[00:05:55] [00:05:55] Mateo: On SOC 2 — is it Type II? And how recent?
[00:05:59] Jordan: We have a SOC 2 Type II report for the period ending 2026-03-31. We'll share a redacted copy.
[00:06:06] Arjun: Redaction is fine but we need to see scope and excluded services called out.
[00:06:10] Priya: We'll ensure scope and the in-scope services are clearly marked.

[00:06:21] [00:06:21] Devon: For Private deployments, what is the timeline to stand up a pilot in our EU VPC?
[00:06:26] Jordan: For a pilot — usually 4-6 weeks depending on networking approvals. There is a template checklist we can send.
[00:06:33] Laura: Any performance or latency impact with customer-managed keys?
[00:06:37] Priya: Minimal for typical requests — there is added latency on key handshake or MK (meta-key) operations during key rotation; token serving uses envelope encryption and cached keys to avoid per-request KMS calls.

[00:06:52] [00:06:52] Arjun: You mentioned cached keys — can that be audited to show key use frequency? We need to demonstrate crypto operations for audits.
[00:06:59] Priya: Yes the KMS usage trail logs key usage events and we can export that. Cached keys are local ephemeral wrapping keys but the master key usage is logged.

[00:07:10] [00:07:10] Jordan: Let's go through a couple of specific SIG items you flagged — section 4 on change management and deployment approvals. Priya, want to cover?
[00:07:18] Priya: Sure. We maintain a change control process with rollbacks and canary deploys. Our console has audit events for each model rollout, and we support canary percentage policies and automatic fallback to last-good. We'll share our deployment playbook.
[00:07:33] Laura: Do you keep immutable snapshots of deployed model binaries for traceability?
[00:07:38] Priya: We keep versioned model artifacts and an immutable metadata record with checksum and provenance.

[00:07:47] [00:07:47] Karen: Procurement — if we need SOC 2 and contract annex, how long to get to signature? We have fiscal deadlines.
[00:07:54] Jordan: If the commercial terms are standard and we can align on data residency, typical procurement cycles for enterprise 3–6 weeks; but evidence delivery doesn't have to wait for signature, we can provision materials now.

[00:08:06] [00:08:06] Mateo: Are you open to adding contractual SLAs around data deletion and breach notification timelines?
[00:08:12] Jordan: Yes, breach notification is standard in our enterprise template, and data deletion windows can be spelled out (subject to the deployment mode).

[00:08:22] [00:08:22] Arjun: On log retention and tamper evidence — do you provide WORM or object lock options?
[00:08:28] Priya: For hosted we offer an archived retention add-on; for dedicated/private we recommend shipping logs to your S3 and then you control object lock/WORM.

[00:08:40] [00:08:40] Laura: A couple of tricky SIG items: 7.2 on subprocessing and vendor governance — can you detail subprocessors and flow?
[00:08:50] Jordan: We'll provide a current subprocessor list with geography, roles, and link to our DPIA. There is also an inbound/outbound data flow diagram.

[00:08:59] [00:08:59] Karen: You mentioned SIEM integration earlier; what formats for log shipping — syslog, API, S3?
[00:09:06] Priya: All three — we can push via syslog/export, or you can pull via signed S3 exports or use API ingestion. We'll include examples for Splunk and Sumo/Elastic.

[00:09:20] [00:09:20] Devon: For the sample logs, can we get them with request/response IDs to test correlation with our tracing?
[00:09:25] Priya: Yes we'll include request IDs.

[00:09:36] [00:09:36] Jordan: Let's cover network isolation questions. For dedicated pools we support private subnets, NAT, and limited egress. For more restrictive environments we can also remove outbound internet access and rely on customer-managed egress proxies.
[00:09:51] Mateo: Are there specific ports or endpoints we need to open?
[00:09:55] Priya: We'll provide a network allowlist with ports and IP ranges.

[00:10:05] [00:10:05] Arjun: On incident response — can we get your playbook and an example post-incident report?
[00:10:11] Jordan: We can share our incident response summary and timeline examples; redacted post-mortems are available.

[00:10:22] [00:10:22] Laura: A compliance detail — ISO 27001 certificate, is that in scope?
[00:10:26] Priya: We maintain ISO 27001 certification for our control plane; we will attach certificate and scope.

[00:10:34] [00:10:34] Devon: Any dependencies on specific cloud providers that would affect our pre-approved list?
[00:10:40] Jordan: We're cloud-agnostic for hosting — we run on major cloud providers. For private we can deploy in your preferred cloud. We'll list supported regions.

[00:10:51] [00:10:51] Arjun: A question about PII handling — can you tag logs to redact PII and do automated redaction?
[00:10:58] Priya: We provide configurable PII redaction at the application layer; customers can also choose not to persist request content. For many regulated customers we recommend tokenization or avoided persistence.

[00:11:12] [00:11:12] Karen: On the evidence intake checklist, our legal team wants to see contractual DPA and subprocessor list with standard SCCs — do you accept SCCs?
[00:11:20] Jordan: Yes we support SCCs and standard DPAs; we'll share the current DPA template.

[00:11:30] [00:11:30] Laura: Are there any known gaps you typically call out during vendor assessments so we can prepare follow-ups?
[00:11:37] Priya: Common items are retention packaging, exact log field samples, and KMS key policy snippets. We find being proactive on those reduces back-and-forth.

[00:11:48] [00:11:48] Devon: For the pilot — can Redwood provide a small dedicated pool so we can run some throughput tests?
[00:11:54] Jordan: Yes we offer reserved pilot capacity for proof-of-concept; we'll put approximate costs in the follow-up.

[00:12:05] [00:12:05] Arjun: Quick micro question — does Redwood store model prompts or customer content by default? We need to know retention and purpose.
[00:12:12] Priya: By default we don't persist customer request content beyond what's needed for debugging; customers can opt-in to retention for caching/quality and that gets clearly marked. Default is minimal ephemeral storage subject to TTLs.

[00:12:25] [00:12:25] Laura: So we need explicit contract clause to ensure PII isn't stored by default.
[00:12:29] Jordan: Noted — we'll highlight that in the DPA and the contract annex.

[00:12:39] [00:12:39] Karen: From procurement standpoint, how do you usually deliver the evidence bundle? Zip, link, or evidence tracker?
[00:12:45] Jordan: We can deliver an indexed zip and concurrently post the items to a secure share with an index spreadsheet; if you prefer a tracker we can populate your template as well.

[00:12:56] [00:12:56] Mateo: A quick note — we also do a secondary review for subprocessors in the EU; we may ask follow-up on any subprocessor outside EU.
[00:13:04] Jordan: Understood, we'll include geography for each subprocessor.

[00:13:14] [00:13:14] Priya: Switching to technical deep-dive items — model artifact provenance and checksuming, we keep an immutable metadata store. It's sometimes transcribed as uh 'K-V' cache in the notes — we support prefix caching and KV cache management for chat workloads.
[00:13:29] Devon: That KV cache — does it store any PII?
[00:13:33] Priya: Cache can be configured to not persist sensitive inputs; for private deployments customers generally prefer ephemeral-only.

[00:13:44] [00:13:44] Arjun: About monitoring and alerting — can you integrate with our PagerDuty and provide SLAs?
[00:13:50] Jordan: Yes we have alert hooks for PagerDuty and can include escalation matrices in the playbook. SLA specifics depend on enterprise tier.

[00:14:01] [00:14:01] Karen: Can you confirm how you log administrative changes to role bindings — we need proof of separation of duty for auditors.
[00:14:09] Priya: Admin role binding changes are logged with actor, timestamp, IP and change diff; we can provide a sample diff export.

[00:14:20] [00:14:20] Jordan: OK — I want to call out a few things we'll deliver: SOC2 redacted, CAIQ crosswalk, ISO cert, KMS key policy snippets, network allowlist, sample audit logs, and sample post-incident report. Does that cover the big asks?
[00:14:34] Laura: Yes that covers most. Also timeline for pilot and data residency confirmations.

[00:14:42] [00:14:42] Devon: On the logs sample — do you have a recommended shredding policy for test data? We can't leak live PII to Redwood.
[00:14:49] Priya: We'll provide fully redacted examples and a redaction checklist. If you want to run a live ingestion test, we recommend synthetic data.

[00:15:00] [00:15:00] Jordan: Let's capture the immediate actions — I'll upload the SOC 2 redacted and CAIQ mapping by Tuesday; Priya will send KMS diagrams and a redacted log sample; Devon will set up staging access and notify us; and we'll schedule the technical deep dive for week of May 18th.

[00:15:18] [00:15:18] Karen: Sounds good. One procurement note — we'll need a list of specific names to call out in contract for subprocessor notifications.
[00:15:25] Jordan: We'll include the current list and a commit to notify of changes within 30 days.

[00:15:34] [00:15:34] Arjun: Small gotcha — SIG question about vulnerability disclosure program and bounty — do you have a program?
[00:15:41] Priya: We have a coordinated disclosure program and work with a third-party bug bounty platform; we'll include the policy link. Sometimes it's transcribed odd as 'bug bunny' in the automated notes.

[00:15:54] [00:15:54] Devon: For KMS integration in private mode, do you support bring-your-own-HSM (BYOH)?
[00:16:00] Priya: We support connection to existing HSMs in the customer's environment where API compatibility exists; we can detail supported vendors.

[00:16:11] [00:16:11] Jordan: All right — I'll pause for any last-minute questions before we move to scheduling the follow-ups.
[00:16:17] Laura: No immediate ones, but appreciate clarity on sample logs and SOC2 redaction.
[00:16:21] Mateo: Same. Confirming timeline for SOC2 share — May 12th works.
[00:16:26] Jordan: Great.

[00:16:30] --- (brief internal sidebar, ~5 minutes, low volume) ---
[00:21:40] [00:21:40] Jordan: Back on track — quick note from CS: we will provide a one-page evidence index to make ingestion easier for procurement.
[00:21:47] Evan: Yep I'll draft the index and share with Karen.

[00:21:55] [00:21:55] Karen: Fantastic, that helps.

[00:22:05] [00:22:05] Arjun: Another compliance question — for change control you said metadata includes checksum; is that signed?
[00:22:12] Priya: Metadata records include hashes and are immutably stored in our metadata store; I can follow up with whether we include signatures or attestations in the export.

[00:22:23] [00:22:23] Devon: For deployment rollbacks — do you keep a retention policy for old models to allow for audits?
[00:22:29] Priya: We keep version history for a configurable window; for audit purposes we can export a snapshot manifest.

[00:22:40] [00:22:40] Jordan: Okay looks like we're wrapping. Recap of agreed next steps: SOC2 (Jordan), KMS diagrams + log sample (Priya), staging access (Devon), evidence index (Evan), schedule tech deep-dive (we'll propose times).
[00:22:58] Laura: We'll review the materials and follow up with any gaps.

[00:23:04] [00:23:04] Mateo: Thanks everyone. Also if we identify show-stoppers we'll surface quickly.
[00:23:09] Jordan: Understood. Appreciate your time. We'll send notes and the initial artifacts in the next 48–72 hours.
[00:23:18] Karen: One last procurement item — can you confirm the contact for legal for NDAs?
[00:23:22] Jordan: Jordan will share, and cc our legal operations contact.
[00:23:26] Priya: Thanks all.
[00:23:30] --- Call ended ---

Call notes / References:
- Redwood SOC 2 Type II (redacted) — link to be provided in follow-up
- CAIQ crosswalk spreadsheet — to be provided
- KMS/HSM architecture diagram — Priya to provide
- Sample audit logs (redacted) — Priya to provide signed URL to staging
- Network allowlist and private deployment checklist — Jordan to provide

Shared artifacts (mentioned, links to follow):
- Evidence index template (Evan)
- DPA and data residency language (Jordan)
- Pilot/reserved capacity cost estimate (Jordan)

End of transcript.
